---
name: to-us
description: Express a user need as clear, testable user stories. Use when a request should be organized around actors, goals, and user-visible value.
---

# Write user stories

A story should connect a real actor and goal to a useful outcome. Use the familiar “As a…, I want…, so that…” structure only when it clarifies those parts; avoid filling it mechanically.

For each story, identify:

- The actor and their relevant permissions or context.
- The action they need to take.
- The outcome and why it matters.
- Acceptance examples, including a meaningful failure or boundary case.

Keep stories small enough to discuss and verify. Separate user-visible behavior from technical enablers, and link enablers to the story they support. Do not treat the story sentence as the entire specification when important rules, data, or compatibility constraints need explicit criteria. Validate terminology with users and avoid assuming that every request maps to one role or one happy path.
